sections.title: Advanced Vocabulary Strategy
sections.content: At Level 3, focus is placed on subtle meanings of words, foreign expressions, and root-based vocabulary. Step 1: Identify the basic meaning and tone of the word. Step 2: If a pair of words is given, understand the relationship between them. Step 3: Recognize Greek or Latin roots or foreign origins. Step 4: Examine the subtle context or emotional nuance. Step 5: Choose the option that gives the most precise meaning.

sections.title: Word Pair Identification
sections.content: Step 1: Understand the meaning of each word separately. Step 2: Determine whether the words have similar meanings (synonyms) or opposite meanings (antonyms). Step 3: Compare their tone and usage. Step 4: Select the pair that clearly shows similarity or opposition. Example: Huge – Enormous (synonyms), Victory – Defeat (antonyms).

sections.title: Foreign Words Used in English
sections.content: Many English words originate from French, Latin, or other languages. Step 1: Identify the origin of the word or phrase. Step 2: Understand its common usage. Step 3: Match it with its correct meaning. Step 4: Imagine how it is used in a sentence. Example: Faux pas = social mistake, Quid pro quo = exchange of favors, Sine qua non = essential condition.

sections.title: Nuanced Shades of Meaning
sections.content: Many words appear similar but carry different emotional shades. Step 1: Understand the basic meaning of both words. Step 2: Identify the difference in attitude or feeling. Step 3: Observe contextual clues in the sentence. Step 4: Select the word that conveys the most accurate nuance. Example: Apathy = lack of interest, Antipathy = strong dislike.

sections.title: Greek and Latin Root Based Words
sections.content: Many complex words are derived from Greek or Latin roots. Step 1: Identify the root word. Step 2: Recall the meaning of the root. Step 3: Look at prefixes or suffixes. Step 4: Estimate the overall meaning of the word. Example: 'Bio' = life, 'Chron' = time, 'Phobia' = fear.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Guessing meaning only from spelling. 2. Interpreting foreign phrases through literal translation. 3. Ignoring subtle emotional differences between close words. 4. Overlooking root meanings.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: At Level 3, deeper vocabulary understanding is required. Recognize relationships in word pairs, understand the meanings of foreign phrases, identify subtle differences in similar words, and use Greek and Latin roots to decode difficult vocabulary.

tricks.title: Pair Meaning Comparison
tricks.explanation: Understand the meaning of both words separately and identify their relationship.

tricks.title: Foreign Phrase Memory
tricks.explanation: Memorize common foreign phrases with their meanings.

tricks.title: Root Word Trick
tricks.explanation: Recognizing roots helps in understanding complex words.

tricks.title: Tone Difference Trick
tricks.explanation: Observe emotional tone differences among close synonyms.
tricks.example: Apathy = no interest, Antipathy = strong dislike.

tricks.title: Prefix Meaning Trick
tricks.explanation: Prefixes often indicate the meaning of the word.

tricks.title: Context Sensitivity Trick
tricks.explanation: Understand the context of the word to determine the correct meaning.
tricks.example: He showed apathy toward the issue.

tricks.title: Elimination Strategy
tricks.explanation: Remove options that clearly do not match the meaning.
tricks.example: If two words clearly share the same meaning, eliminate unrelated options.

tricks.title: Foreign Phrase Usage Check
tricks.explanation: Check the situation in which the phrase is used.
tricks.example: Quid pro quo → something given in return.
